title: Seamless VPC runtime hot-swap orchestrator with canary health automation
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement an orchestrator and IaC workflow to perform zero-downtime hot-swap upgrades of Private (VPC) data plane runtimes. This ticket covers the end-to-end automation: Terraform module changes, canary traffic steering, health scoring, KV cache priming/mirroring, graceful connection drain, and an automated rollback path that reverts infra and runtime in a safe order. Goal: enable teams to push runtime and kernel-level changes across multi-AZ Private deployments without customer-visible errors or significant latency spikes.
acceptance_criteria: New orchestrator can perform an in-place rolling upgrade across all AZs while maintaining request success rate >= 99.5% and P95 latency regression < 15% for a representative workload
Canary stepper supports configurable % traffic increments, min-stable-duration, and automatic promotion/rollback based on health score
KV cache priming job reduces cache-miss rate on canary pods by >= 60% compared to cold-start baseline
Terraform module updates are reversible: state lock, module version pin, and apply/rollback playbooks exist and are exercised in staging
Automated rollback completes within the same maintenance window and restores previous metrics to within 5% of pre-upgrade baseline
Runbook and on-call playbooks linked in Confluence with exact CLI commands and required dashboards
implementation_plan: Design orchestrator flow: leader elect -> sequence AZ by AZ -> within-AZ canary -> drain -> promote
Terraform: introduce module private/runtime-orchestrator v0.3.0 with inputs for canary config, health thresholds, and module_version lockfile
Controller: Kubernetes operator (or control-plane service) implements canary stepper, health aggregation, and rollback trigger hooks
Traffic control: integrate with envoy sidecar control plane to do % splits, mirroring for shadow validation, and connection drain (graceful timeout)
KV cache: add priming job that replays recent prefixes and warm KV across canary nodes before promotion
Observability: new Grafana dashboard + derived metrics (aggregate health score, priming success rate, regression delta) and PagerDuty runbook
Security & compliance: KMS key rotation handling and ensure secretless bootstrap for orchestrator in VPC private control plane
infra_changes: Terraform module: registry.redwood/internal/private-runtime-orchestrator v0.3.0 (adds canary_config, leader_election, lockfile support)
Add IAM role for orchestrator service principal: allow read/write to S3 state, KMS decrypt, and tag-based rollout permissions
GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime-operator/pull/78 (operator canary stepper + health aggregation)
Add CI job: apply-plan-staging that validates module upgrades against a mock VPC stack
test_plan: Staging run: perform full upgrade on staging cluster with synthetic traffic generator (mix of short-chat, long-chat, and embeddings) and validate SLOs
Chaos: inject node termination and network latency during canary to ensure orchestrator retries and fallback behavior
Priming validation: measure KV cache hit ratio pre/post priming and ensure priming jobs do not exceed allotted CPU/GPU budget
Security test: verify orchestrator cannot escalate privileges and KMS access is scoped
Dry-run terraform apply/rollback executed and recorded (integration test)
rollback_plan: Automatic rollback trigger: health score falls below threshold for configured min_stable_duration -> orchestrator initiates revert

Rollback steps: (1) stop promotion, (2) shift traffic back to previous nodes, (3) re-enable draining on upgraded nodes and mark for automated reprovision or investigate, (4) terraform apply with previous module_version lockfile to revert infra changes
State concerns: ensure S3 statefile backup and restore point created before each plan; use feature-flag to disable automatic state pruning
Manual override: on-call can execute 'private-upgrade rollback --from=canary --to=previous' documented in runbook
Post-rollback validation: run smoke tests, synthetic latency checks, and an eval prompt-set to ensure quality
metrics_and_alerts: Health score = weighted(availability(50%), error_rate(30%), p95_latency(20%)) computed per canary cohort
Alert: upgrade.health_drop > 5% sustained for min_stable_duration -> P0 pager
Alert: cache_miss_rate_increase > 40% on canary -> annotate and possibly rollback
notes_and_tradeoffs: Choosing mirroring over full shadow traffic avoids doubled cost for long-running tests but reduces fidelity for tail-stateful bugs
Aggressive priming reduces visible regressions but may increase transient load on GPUs; we limit priming to configured CPU/GPU budget per AZ
We prefer infra-first rollback (terraform apply revert) only when operator cannot reach a consistent runtime state; otherwise prefer runtime-level rollback to reduce infra churn
Leader election for orchestrator increases safety but adds a single control-plane role that must be secured and audited
